races.title: State Assembly, District 47
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Greg Wallis
cands.bio: Republican member of the California State Assembly for District 47 since December 2022. Earlier he was district director for Assemblymember Chad Mayes, an account executive at Mann Communications, and executive director of the Inland Empire Taxpayers Association. He studied political science at California Lutheran University.

endorsements.text: Reform California listed among his 2026 endorsements and voter guide recommendations.
Republican Party of California endorsed him in 2024.

cands.gaps: His birthplace and where he grew up were not found, so his ties to California cannot be scored beyond his own description as a third-generation Californian who settled in the Coachella Valley over a decade ago. We found no documented stands on data centers, development, homestead property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, H-1B and immigration enforcement, gun policy, or abortion. His campaign site speaks to schools and public safety only in general terms and does not name specific bills. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in any year.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.
score.why_money: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since December 2022, serving on the Budget, Utilities and Energy, and Governmental Organization committees, and vice-chair of the Insurance Committee. Before that he was a district director for Assemblymember Chad Mayes, executive director of the Inland Empire Taxpayers Association, and an account executive at Mann Communications.
qual.why: He has held legislative office since 2022, including a seat on the Budget Committee, and earlier worked as legislative district staff and at a taxpayer-policy association. Committee seats were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: He has held legislative office since 2022, including a seat on the Budget Committee, and earlier worked as legislative district staff and at a taxpayer-policy association. Committee seats were not counted toward the score.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: His campaign site says he continued making it easier for parents to move students from failing schools into good public or charter schools, and that he fought to pay teachers well and reform tenure. It gives no specific raise amount.

back-police-order.evidence: His campaign site says he fights the "Defund the Police" movement and voted to toughen penalties on fentanyl dealers and on sexual predators who prey on children. It also says he is working to restore tough penalties for violent and property crimes. The site does not name specific bills.

prio.label: Matches 2 of 2 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 2 only promised

cands.name: Leila Namvar
cands.bio: Labor leader and city employee running for Assembly District 47 as a Democrat. Born in Iran, she has worked for the City of Indio since 2005, from Planning Technician to Public Arts Program Analyst. She was Chapter President of SEIU 721 at the City of Indio.

endorsements.text: California Federation of Labor Unions, AFL-CIO; California Nurses Association; National Union of Healthcare Workers; California Young Democrats; San Bernardino Young Democrats (listed by Ballotpedia)
Planned Parenthood Action Fund of the Pacific Southwest (stated on her campaign site)

cands.gaps: We could not find her birth city, the year she moved to California, or her education. She has held no elected office, so there are no votes or official actions to report. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no stated positions on property taxes, institutional or foreign land buyers, growth limits, policing, gun laws, school choice or teacher pay. Her campaign site's statement on housing is general. We found no news coverage or controversies about her. Her work history comes only from her campaign site.

local.label: Roots 40: She was born and raised in Iran, came to the U.S. as an adult in 2002, and her campaign site says she has worked for the City of Indio since 2005, about 21 years; the date she moved to California is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: City of Indio employee since 2005, starting as a Planning Technician and becoming a Public Arts Program Analyst. She says she helped shape strategic plans and manage city budgets. She was Chapter President of SEIU 721 at the City of Indio and led contract negotiations three times. She has held no elected office.
qual.why: Local-government planning and budget work plus union negotiating experience puts her in the middle band; she has no prior legislative service, and the details come from her own campaign site.
qual.label: Local-government planning and budget work plus union negotiating experience puts her in the middle band; she has no prior legislative service, and the details come from her own campaign site.

stop-data-centers.evidence: Says she will block new data centers that don't sign community benefit agreements with local hiring requirements, and limit them to existing industrial areas away from schools and homes. This is a restriction, not a ban.

pro-life.evidence: Campaign site lists protecting abortion rights as a top issue and says she is endorsed by Planned Parenthood Action Fund of the Pacific Southwest because she will protect women's reproductive freedom.

workers-first.evidence: Says she will fight back against ICE and protect communities from harmful federal immigration actions.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: She was born and raised in Iran, came to the U.S. as an adult in 2002, and her campaign site says she has worked for the City of Indio since 2005, about 21 years; the date she moved to California is not stated.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: Says data centers affect local electricity and water costs and the environment. She would block new data centers that don't sign community benefit agreements with local hiring requirements, and limit them to existing industrial areas away from schools and homes.
